newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Shanghai newspapers - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Shanghai newspapers - July 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major political and business stories in local newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Shanghai. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- SHANGHAI SECURITIES NEWS - Efforts to reform state-owned enterprises are showing success, as assets of the 100 state firms being reformed nationally hit 360 billion yuan by the end of 1996, up 27.6 percent from the end of 1994.
- A total of 9,763 foreign-funded firms were approved to do business in China in the first half of 1997, down 30.57 percent compared with the same 1996 period.
- China's futures market shows signs of recovery in July after sluggish trading in the first half of 1997, with turnover of some major contracts rising sharply.
- BUSINESS NEWS - Prominent economist Xiao Zhuoji says foreign currency B shares should be opened to domestic investors.
- Chinese production of IC cards is set to surpass 40 million in 1997, up 170 percent from 1996, but the IC card market is chaotic and needs regulation.
- Trade between Shanghai and Taiwan reached $595 million in the first half of 1997, up 8.9 percent compared with the same 1996 period.
